# RunnerCard

> RunnerCard is a collectible walking game for iPhone (iOS 17+, currently in
> TestFlight beta). Every day, a few large zones land on public parks and
> walkable trails near the player — never on private or government land.
> Walking 1 km inside a zone (GPS-verified, walking pace or faster) mints a
> collectible Runner Card stamped with the distance, steps and date that
> earned it. Free to play, and runner data is stored on the phone first.

Key facts:

- Platform: iPhone only, iOS 17+ (TestFlight beta); no Android version
- Price: free to play; cards have no monetary value and cannot be bought or sold
- Cards: 5 types — Gem (valuable), Gear (equip), Creature (wild), Artifact
  (unseen, first-finder credited), Fact (knowledge, collected into decks)
- Rarities and published odds: Common ~6 in 10, Uncommon ~1 in 4, Rare
  ~1 in 12, Epic ~1 in 60, Legendary ~1 in 900
- Zones: 2–4 per day, large circles (roughly 350–500 m radius) anchored on
  public parks and clusters of walkable trails, picked fresh daily; zones are
  never placed on private property, private land, or government land
  (OpenStreetMap no-go polygons are vetoed fail-closed)
- Mint rule: cover 1 km inside a zone while the app is open on the map or
  during a run; distance is GPS-verified — accuracy worse than 50 m never
  counts, teleports are rejected, and driving-speed movement fills nothing;
  up to 3 mints per zone per day
- Tracking: distance, per-km splits, pace and day streaks on every run;
  syncs with Apple Health on-device
- Privacy: local-first storage on the iPhone; Apple Health data is never
  uploaded; location permission is "While Using" only — position is used on
  the map and during runs to measure distance inside zones, with no
  background tracking
- Map data: © OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL)
- Contact: hey@runnercard.app
